title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
claim: Eu3+ emission is a particularly useful local-structure probe: Stark-component counts, relative intensities, line energies, and decay curves report site multiplicity, coordinated water, local symmetry, ligand-field magnitude, covalency, and nearby vibrations.
explanation: Because 4f transitions are inner-shell but still sensitive to the ligand field, changes in the emission manifold and excited-state kinetics are interpreted as coordination information. The review lists these observables as standard for Ln3+ environments and singles out Eu3+.
scope: Ln3+ complexes, especially Eu3+ as a spectroscopic probe of the local coordination sphere.
conditions: Analysis of intra-4f manifolds, including excitation-wavelength and temperature dependence and decay curves.
caveats: The section presents this as a general spectroscopic capability, not as a demonstrated SMM design rule for Eu3+ itself.
